title: Coding-Assistant Token Spend with Tokenomics
dataSources: Spend reported by the coding-assistant providers to Tokenomics, joined to a Workday directory; daily refresh, no backfill
description: Reports coding-assistant spend and adoption across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Windsurf with Splunk Agent Observability Tokenomics, joined to the Workday directory.
value: Engineering leaders need to see which teams use which coding assistants and what they spend. Tokenomics answers that without touching agent traces.
implementation: Connect the coding-assistant providers and the Workday directory to Tokenomics. Review spend by team monthly. Use per-trace cost (UC-13.8.35) for this organisation's own agents; Tokenomics does not read agent traces.
visualization: Tokenomics spend by team and provider.
knownFalsePositives: Data refreshes daily with no backfill, so history starts the day the provider is connected. Read-only users see nothing; managers and users see their team.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

No agent instrumentation. Tokenomics reads provider-reported spend, not traces.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Set up the provider connections and the Workday directory join in Tokenomics, following the Tokenomics documentation.

Step 3 — Validate

After the first daily refresh, confirm spend appears per team for each connected provider. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Review spend by team monthly with the engineering budget owner.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No history before go-live: there is no backfill. A manager sees only their team: that is the documented visibility.
grandmaExplanation: We see how much each team spends on the coding helpers their engineers use, so budgets match real use.

productArtifacts.title: Tokenomics coding-assistant spend review
productArtifacts.body:
Providers: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf
Directory: Workday
Refresh: daily, no backfill
Visibility: admin sees the org; manager and user see their team; read-only sees nothing
Scope: coding-assistant adoption only. It does not read this organisation's agent traces; do not add it to per-trace cost.
